tasks.title: Make task orchestration an explicit state machine
tasks.description: The planned LangGraph migration is directionally right, but the first implementation should stay tightly scoped to task lifecycle orchestration. Model planned -> build-started -> cba-complete -> build-finished -> PR-Reviewed-> staged -> production as persisted graph state with formal human gates, proof gates, retry paths, and failure recovery. Use this to replace implicit skill-driven transitions with explicit preconditions, transition rules, and resumable state.
tasks.plan:
## Overview

Task #24 shipped LangGraph stubs (state.py, task_graph.py, task_executor.py). Task #26 makes the state machine authoritative: formal preconditions, real HITL pause/resume, proof gate verification, retry paths, failure recovery, and a sync contract with backlog.json so both existing skills and new LangGraph nodes stay in sync.

## Phases

1. Extend TaskState — add proof_units, proof_results, human_gate_signal, retry_count, error_log, StatusLiteral matching backlog enum
2. Formal Transition Table — transitions.py with preconditions and mutations for each (from, to) pair
3. Real HITL Pause/Resume — executor actually suspends at interrupt nodes; /signal unblocks; stall timeout sets status=stalled
4. Proof Gates and Retry Paths — finish_build_node validates proof units; codex_review retry edge; failed_smoke dead-end node
5. Failure Recovery — @safe_node decorator snapshots state and sets status=failed on exception
6. backlog.json Sync Contract — executor writes status back after each node; /sync-state endpoint in server.js

## First Proof Unit

tasks.title: Replace regex-heavy tool safety with capability policies
tasks.description: Polaris already has thoughtful file, shell, installer, worktree, size, and encoding safeguards, but several critical protections depend on command regexes and scattered checks. Introduce normalized capability policy objects that define allowed roots, write modes, network permissions, installer permission, destructive command classes, and per-session trust levels. Make tool execution evaluate these policies before running commands or writes, and emit structured audit events for privileged actions.
tasks.plan:
## Overview

Replace scattered regex-based tool safety checks with a unified CapabilityPolicy system. Each agent session gets a frozen policy object at launch. Tool execution evaluates the policy before running any command or write. Privileged actions emit structured audit events to a JSONL file and the UI.

## Phases

1. Policy schema + session wiring — CapabilityPolicy type, buildDefaultPolicy() factory, session attachment
2. Command class registry — replace SHELL_HARD_BLOCKED regex array with named class registry + structural detection
3. evaluatePolicy unified enforcer — single function replacing assertWritable + assertSafeCommand + detectInstallerExe
4. Audit emission — append events to audit.jsonl, emit tool-audit WebSocket message for blocks and grants
5. Wire into tool execution — replace call sites in toolBash, toolPowerShell, toolWrite, toolEdit; consolidate duplicate shell precheck
6. Unit test suite — one test per command class, write boundary check, and installer gate

## Subtasks

Task #41: Capability policy schema + session wiring
Task #42: Command class registry
Task #43: evaluatePolicy unified enforcer
Task #44: Audit JSONL + WebSocket event
Task #45: Wire policy into tool execution
Task #46: Policy unit test suite

Audit events appended to audit.jsonl and emitted as tool-audit WebSocket message for every block and grant

tasks.title: Capability policy schema + session wiring
tasks.description: Define the CapabilityPolicy TypeScript type with fields: allowedRoots (string[]), writeMode ('read-only'|'project-only'|'extended'), networkAllowed (boolean), installerAllowed (boolean), blockedCommandClasses (string[]), trustLevel ('restricted'|'standard'|'elevated'). Add a buildDefaultPolicy(session, config) factory that reads workDir, obsidianVaultPath, and downloadsDir once at session creation and returns a frozen policy object. Attach the policy to the session object at session launch.

tasks.title: Command class registry for shell safety
tasks.description: Replace the SHELL_HARD_BLOCKED regex array in server.js with a COMMAND_CLASS_REGISTRY map. Each entry has a name (e.g. GIT_FORCE_PUSH, GIT_RESET_HARD, GIT_CLEAN, DRIVE_FORMAT, RM_RECURSIVE_ROOT, RD_FULL_DRIVE), a detect(command) function that may combine regex with structural path analysis, and a minimumTrustLevel field. The registry is the single source of truth for what constitutes a destructive command class.

tasks.title: evaluatePolicy unified enforcer
tasks.description: Write evaluatePolicy(action, context, policy): PolicyResult in server.js (or src/runtime/capabilityPolicy.ts if the toolRuntime module is wired). Handles: root boundary check (replaces assertWritable path logic), command class evaluation using COMMAND_CLASS_REGISTRY (replaces assertSafeCommand), installer gate (replaces detectInstallerExe + async approval prompt). Returns { allowed: boolean, reason?: string, auditEvent: AuditEvent }. Does not throw — callers inspect the result and throw if !allowed.

tasks.title: Audit JSONL + tool-audit WebSocket event
tasks.description: On every evaluatePolicy call, append a structured event to %APPDATA%\.claude\polaris\audit.jsonl. Event schema: { ts, sessionId, action, tool, allowed, reason, commandSnippet }. Also emit a tool-audit WebSocket broadcast message for any block or grant (allowed=false or installerAllowed action). The JSONL file is append-only; no pruning in this task.

tasks.title: Wire evaluatePolicy into tool execution
tasks.description: Replace assertWritable + assertSafeCommand + detectInstallerExe call sites in toolBash, toolPowerShell, toolWrite, and toolEdit with evaluatePolicy. Consolidate the duplicated shell precheck sequence (assertSafeCommand + detectInstallerExe + detectShellWriteTargets + backupBeforeWrite + snapshotForShellEncodingCheck) that currently appears identically in both toolBash and toolPowerShell into a single shellPrecheck(command, workDir, sessionId, policy) helper. No behavior changes — enforcement must be identical to what existed before.

tasks.title: Policy unit test suite
tasks.description: Write unit tests for evaluatePolicy covering: one test per COMMAND_CLASS_REGISTRY entry (each class is blocked at standard trust level), write boundary check (path outside allowedRoots is denied), extended write mode allows Obsidian path, installer gate blocks when installerAllowed=false, installer gate allows when installerAllowed=true. Tests should run without a live server — evaluatePolicy must be importable in isolation.

tasks.title: Expand agent evals into product-critical acceptance suites
tasks.description: The existing agent eval harness is a strong seed, but it is too small to guard Polaris's behavior as the system grows. Add suites for tool choice, permission refusal, QueryMemory fallback, Cross-Check approval and rejection, backlog transitions, model regressions, latency, token cost, retry behavior, and failure recovery. Report pass rate, tool-call count, token use, latency, and regression deltas in concise scorecards.

tasks.title: Make trust, proof, cost, and recovery visible in the product
tasks.description: Polaris's strongest product idea is an AI command center with trust rails, not just parallel agent sessions. Bring task state, proof state, risk state, Cross-Check state, and cost state into a clearer first-class workflow surface. Add explanations for why a session is waiting, one-click recovery from failed gates, and a guided task lane for plan, build, review, stage, and production promotion.

tasks.title: Add a ship task orchestration capability.
tasks.description: I want to have an orchestration window that monitors all open active sessions for projects and ensures that coordination and conflicts are managed. Reference this file for more information.   docs/orchestrator-design.md
tasks.plan:
## Overview

Add an orchestrator window that auto-activates when two or more sessions are open for the same project. The orchestrator is a passive monitor — it reads session state, detects conflicts, and enables Scott to resolve conflicts and push git/Obsidian updates per session. No commands run from the orchestrator directly.

## Phases

1. Server Foundations: Session registry + 4 new HTTP endpoints (GET /branch-state, POST /reserve-merge-slot, POST /release-merge-slot, POST /dry-run-merge stub). Persist state to orchestrator-state.json in Runtime zone.
2. Git Integration: Worktree state query helper, file contention detection, full dry-run merge implementation (throwaway branch, auto-cleaned).
3. Orchestrator UI Panel: New panel in mockup.html — auto-activates on second session, session cards with branch/worktree/conflict state, push buttons.
4. Conflict Resolution + Merge Serialization: FIFO merge slot queue wired into push flow, Obsidian bridge for session summaries, retry logic, amber conflict alerts.

## First Proof Unit

GET /branch-state returns live session data. curl http://localhost:40000/branch-state returns HTTP 200 with JSON containing featureBranches keyed by branch name with head, worktreePath, and contention fields.

tasks.plan:
## Overview

Create the Zod contracts foundation for Polaris. Four modules in src/contracts/: ws-messages.ts (all WebSocket message types), backlog.ts (BacklogTask schema + BacklogStatus enum), tools.ts (all 14 native tool schemas), mcp.ts (MCPServer + MCPToolEnvelope). Barrel-exported via index.ts.

## Phases

1. Add zod to package.json dependencies and run npm install.
2. Create src/contracts/backlog.ts - BacklogStatus enum and BacklogTask schema.
3. Create src/contracts/tools.ts - schemas for all 14 native tools.
4. Create src/contracts/mcp.ts - MCPServer, MCPToolEnvelope schemas.
5. Create src/contracts/ws-messages.ts - Zod schemas for all WebSocket message types.
6. Create src/contracts/index.ts - barrel re-export of all four modules.
7. Run npx tsc --noEmit and fix any errors.

objective.statement: Create runtime-validatable Zod schemas as the contracts foundation for Polaris — four modules in src/contracts/ covering WebSocket messages, backlog tasks, native tools, and MCP envelopes — with a barrel export and a clean tsc --noEmit.
successCriteria: Zod is in package.json dependencies and installed
src/contracts/ws-messages.ts exports Zod schemas for all WebSocket message types
src/contracts/backlog.ts exports BacklogTask schema and BacklogStatus enum as Zod
src/contracts/tools.ts exports all 14 native tool schemas as Zod
src/contracts/mcp.ts exports MCPServer and MCPToolEnvelope schemas as Zod

tasks.title: Wire runtime validation: use compiled contracts in server.js
tasks.description: Add tsc build step to package.json scripts so contracts compile to dist/contracts/. In server.js, replace hand-rolled backlog validation (VALID_BACKLOG_STATUSES, _validImpact, field checks) with compiled Zod validators. Add WebSocket receive-side validation so malformed messages are rejected with a structured error. No changes to business logic — validation only.

tasks.title: Registry generation: generate docs/registries/ from schemas
tasks.description: Write scripts/generate-registries.js that imports compiled contract modules from dist/contracts/ and generates docs/registries/websocket-messages.md, backlog-task-fields.md, tool-schemas.md, and mcp-envelopes.md. Add npm script "generate:registries". Run it to regenerate all current registries and verify output matches existing hand-written content.

tasks.title: Contract test suite: validate real payload samples
tasks.description: Write test/contracts/ test files. Each file covers one contract module: valid samples pass, invalid samples produce descriptive Zod errors. Add npm script "test:contracts". Covers ws-messages, backlog tasks, tool calls, and MCP envelopes.
